title: Dubai Little Explorers | Dubai Holiday Package for Children
meta_description: Let your kids enjoy Dubai with this child-friendly Dubai holiday package for Children featuring fun attractions, activities, and a comfortable family stay.
content: Dubai Little Explorers | Dubai Holiday Package for ChildrenHelplineEnglish / AEDHomeHolidaysDubai CityDubai Little Explorers Kids Holiday PackageShareAdd to Wishlist5N / 6D3 ImagesView GalleryDubai Little Explorers Kids Holiday PackageNewHotelsSightseeingEntry TicketsMealsActivitiesTransfersOverviewDubai tour packages that focus on kids’ attractions are exactly what family holidaymakers want. Tailor-made for children, pre-teens, and teenagers, our Dubai kids adventure package offers a balanced mix of adventure, thrill, and chill. Besides exploring Dubai’s breathtaking wonders and family-friendly desert adventures, kids can have fun at the Dubai Mall’s attractions like KidZania and Play DXB. Enjoy a splashy family time at the Wild Wadi Water Park, and marvel at the virtual world of AYA Universe. You also get one full day to plan and enjoy a theme park or other attractions.  With comfortable, breakfast-inclusive accommodations, stress-free private airport transfers, and visits to attractions handled smoothly, watch your children discover why Dubai is the world’s ultimate destination for fun.ItineraryDay 1Arrival in Dubai, Dubai Marina Dhow Cruise with DinnerAfter arrival in Dubai, you will be transferred to your hotel in a private car. Once you check in, take some time to relax. In the evening, enjoy your first Dubai family outing with your children at the Dubai Marina. Hop on a dhow cruise to admire the scintillating waterfront views and relish a sumptuous dinner onboard. This is the perfect, gentle start to your holiday, offering plenty of photo opportunities. After the cruise, head back to your hotel for a good night’s sleep so that you can be ready for tomorrow’s big adventure!Day 2Half-Day Dubai City Tour and Dubai Mall Attractions (Dubai Aquarium, KidZania, and Play DXB)Fuel up for the day with a wholesome breakfast at the hotel and gear up for a day of exciting thrills. Start your morning by exploring the city on a half-day Dubai city tour. Cruise past famous landmarks like the Jumeirah Mosque, Palm Jumeirah, and Burj Al Arab. The city tour ends with a drop-off at the Dubai Mall. Here, you and the kids can enjoy an exciting time spotting exotic sea creatures up close at the Dubai Aquarium and Underwater Zoo or gaming at Play DXB. You can also let your kids enjoy their time acting like grown-ups at KidZania, while you explore the other wonders of this colossal mall. After a day filled with excitement, head back to the hotel on a shared transfer for an overnight stay.Day 3Evening Dubai Desert Safari Experience with BBQ DinnerEnjoy your breakfast and relax for the rest of the day. In the late afternoon, zoom off to the vast deserts of Dubai for an adventurous time. Your Dubai desert safari tour features a milder dune-bashing experience suitable for children, followed by sandboarding and camel rides.  At dusk, pose for some family pictures with a stellar sunset backdrop. After a lavish BBQ dinner, live entertainment, and Tanoura shows, transfer back to the hotel for an overnight stay.Day 4Dubai Frame, AYA Universe, and Wild Wadi Water ParkAfter breakfast, spend the day at the Dubai Frame, where you will stare wide-eyed at the glistening, colossal frame dominating the scenery. Enjoy unrivaled panoramas of Old Dubai and the modern city from its observation deck. Next, visit AYA Universe, an immersive, multi-sensory experience with touch-responsive installations, virtual zones, and interactive creative projections that make you feel like you have landed in an otherworldly realm. Finally, Wild Wadi Waterpark welcomes you to spend the remainder of the day sliding down exciting water rides and splashing in pools. Though it may be a tiring day, the happy, content smiles of your kids during the transfer back to the hotel guarantee that the day was worthwhile. Catch up on sleep at the hotel to be ready and refreshed for another day in Dubai.Day 5Day Free at LeisureAfter breakfast, enjoy a day free of any scheduled activities. Explore a theme park or visit a favorite Dubai attraction on your own. This is a great option if you do not want to overwhelm your trip or prefer to enjoy it as one of the most affordable family vacation deals to Dubai. title: Ultimate Dubai Explorer Package | Best of Dubai and Abu Dhabi
meta_description: Discover Dubai’s major attractions with this Ultimate Explorer Dubai package — perfect for Best of Dubai and Abu Dhabi experience.
content: Ultimate Dubai Explorer Package | Best of Dubai and Abu DhabiHelplineEnglish / AEDHomeHolidaysDubai CityUltimate Dubai ExplorerShareAdd to Wishlist5N / 6D3 ImagesView GalleryUltimate Dubai ExplorerNewHotelsSightseeingEntry TicketsMealsActivitiesTransfersOverviewGear up for the ultimate holiday experience with the best of Dubai-Abu Dhabi tour packages. Designed for families, couples, and groups, this tour package offers the best of Dubai and Abu Dhabi, the most popular Emirates of the UAE. Venture into the UAE’s cultural, adventurous, luxurious, and architectural aspects with one of the well-curated 5-night Dubai packages tours.ItineraryDay 1Arrival & Dhow Cruise DinnerThis is one of the best sightseeing tour packages of Dubai and Abu Dhabi, beginning with your arrival in Dubai, with a private vehicle and driver waiting for you at the Dubai International Airport. Once at the hotel, you check in, refresh, relax, and get ready for an evening cruising on a traditional dhow at Dubai Marina. Enjoy the cool winds, delicious food, and the sights of the glamorous Dubai Marina on the dhow cruise.Day 2City Tour, Burj Khalifa, and Downtown DubaiBegin your second day in the city with our city tour. Get comfortable in our tour vehicle as it takes you to the city’s key attractions and landmarks of Dubai before dropping you off at Burj Khalifa. Hop on to the fastest elevator in the world to reach “At the Top” of Burj Khalifa. Located on the 124th and 125th floors of the tallest building in the world, you get to enjoy a panoramic view of the city. Next is the Dubai Mall, where you see marine life in the Dubai Aquarium & Underwater Zoo and have a fun time at House of Hype. Do not forget to check out the Dubai Fountain Show right outside the mall.Day 3Evening Desert SafariAfter a day of sightseeing, take time to relax and rest your legs. Alternatively, you can also explore the city on your own. But be ready by late afternoon to head out to Dubai’s desert for the desert safari experience. An array of activities and attractions awaits you at the desert camp. Enjoy a dune-bashing session, followed by desert safari experiences like camel riding, sandboarding, and quad biking. Watch a sunset and let the performers entertain you with belly dance, Tanoura dance, and fire shows, while you savor a 3-course BBQ dinner.Day 4A Trip to Abu DhabiAs this is one of the best tour packages of two emirates, you get to spend an entire day in Abu Dhabi, exploring its marvels. The tour begins from your Dubai hotel and takes you to all the attractions of the UAE capital. The guided tour will take you to the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, Heritage Village, Corniche, Emirates Palace, and more before dropping you off at your hotel in Dubai in the evening.Day 5IMG Worlds of AdventureSpend the last day of your Dubai-Abu Dhabi explorer package at the IMG Worlds of Adventure, the world’s largest indoor theme park. With six zones and 22 signature rides, this theme park is the perfect place to hang out with your friends and family. IMG Worlds also has plenty of restaurants, cafes, and retail stores. After a day at IMG Worlds, you can spend the rest of the day exploring the city more, shopping for souvenirs and gifts, or trying out the variety of foods available here.Day 6Fly Back HomeAfter breakfast at your hotel, head over to the Dubai Airport in our private vehicle to catch your flight back home.Hotel OptionsAsiana Hotel or SimilarKnight Castle Hotel or SimilarKnight Castle Hotel or Best Time to Visit Ras Al Khaimah The best time to visit Ras Al Khaimah is during the cooler months from November to March. During this period, the temperatures are more moderate, typically ranging from 18°C to 25°C (64°F to 77°F), making it perfect for outdoor activities like hiking in the rugged Hajjar Mountains, lounging on pristine beaches, or exploring the historical sites scattered across the region. But the summer months from June to September, when temperatures can soar above 40°C (104°F), could not be the best time to be outdoors.. While this intense heat can limit outdoor exploration, the emirate is well-equipped with indoor attractions and amenities. Quick Guide Top Attractions Ras Al Khaimah is renowned for its stunning landscapes, cultural heritage, and adventurous opportunities. Here are some of the top attractions you shouldn't miss when visiting this captivating emirate: 1.	Jebel Jais: As the highest peak in the United Arab Emirates, Jebel Jais offers breathtaking views and thrilling activities. Visitors can enjoy the Jebel Jais Flight, the world’s longest zipline, providing an adrenaline-pumping experience. The cooler temperatures and stunning vistas make it perfect for hiking and picnics. 2.	Al Hamra Village: A picturesque development featuring traditional architecture, Al Hamra Village combines modern living with a historical feel. Its beautifully designed golf course, marina, and lush landscapes attract both residents and tourists. It's also home to Al Hamra Mall, offering shopping, dining, and entertainment options. 3.	Dhayah Fort: For a taste of history, Dhayah Fort is a must-see. This 18th-century fort is the last hilltop fort in the UAE and played a crucial role in the region's defense. Visitors can climb to the top for panoramic views of the surrounding mangroves and mountains. 4.	Ras Al Khaimah National Museum: Housed in a historic fort, the Ras Al Khaimah National Museum offers insights into the emirate’s history and culture. The museum's exhibits showcase a range of artifacts, including ancient pottery, traditional weapons, and documents that tell the story of the area’s evolution. 5.	Al Jazirah Al Hamra: Often referred to as the "ghost town," Al Jazirah Al Hamra is an abandoned pearling village that offers a glimpse into the past. Wander through its winding streets and explore the remnants of coral-stone buildings, mosques, and market areas preserved in time. 6. Saqr Park: Perfect for families, Saqr Park is the largest public park in Ras Al Khaimah. It offers green spaces for picnics, playgrounds, and a variety of recreational facilities, making it a great place for relaxation and family activities. 7.	Shimal: A fascinating archaeological site located north of Ras Al Khaimah, Shimal is home to ancient tombs and settlements dating back to the Bronze and Iron Ages. Visitors interested in archaeology will find this site intriguing for its historical significance and ongoing excavations. 8.	Iceland Water Park: For a day of fun-filled aquatic adventures, Iceland Water Park offers a wide array of slides, wave pools, and attractions. It's a great spot for families and thrill-seekers looking to beat the desert heat. 9.	Al Marjan Island: This man-made marvel is perfect for beach lovers and water sports enthusiasts. 10.	Khatt Springs: It’s renowned for its therapeutic hot springs set amidst mineral-rich mountains. Culture Ras Al Khaimah’s cultural background is a mesmerizing blend of ancient heritage and modern dynamism. It offers cultural enthusiasts a chance to explore the depth and diversity of Emirati culture, while its historical sites provide a rich narrative of the region's past. As the emirate continues to grow, it stands as a testament to the harmonious coexistence of tradition and modernity, making it a compelling destination for cultural exploration. Cuisine Emirati cuisine in Ras Al Khaimah is a celebration of rich flavors and aromatic spices. That said, Ras Al Khaimah’s culinary scene reflects its cosmopolitan population, offering cuisines from around the world. From authentic Italian trattorias and French bistros to bustling Indian curry houses and modern fusion eateries, the emirate caters to varied palates. This diversity is particularly visible in the bustling dining scene at Al Hamra Village and Marjan Island. Practical Tips The currency in the United Arab Emirates is the Dirham (AED). Top Things to Do in Ras Al Khaimah Ras Al Khaimah, one of the hidden gems of the United Arab Emirates, offers a delightful mix of adventure, culture, and natural beauty. Whether you're a thrill-seeker, history enthusiast, or nature lover, there's something for everyone in this captivating emirate. Here are some top things you should consider doing during your visit: 1.	Experience the World's Longest Zipline: Jebel Jais, part of the stunning Hajjar Mountains, is not only the UAE's highest peak but also home to the Jebel Jais Flight, the world’s longest zipline. Here, you can soar at speeds of 120-150 kph while enjoying breathtaking views of rugged mountains. 2.	Hiking and Scenic Drives : For those who prefer to stay grounded, Jebel Jais offers numerous hiking trails and scenic drives that provide panoramic views and the opportunity to bask in the tranquility of nature. 3.	Explore Al Jazirat Al Hamra: Step back in time at Al Jazirat Al Hamra, one of the UAE’s last surviving traditional towns. This abandoned fishing village offers a hauntingly beautiful glimpse into life in the pre-oil era with its coral-stone houses and deserted souks. 4.	Relax at the Beaches: Ras Al Khaimah is blessed with serene beaches perfect for relaxation and various water activities. Whether you're looking to lounge under the sun, swim in the azure waters, or try your hand at kayaking and paddleboarding, the beaches here provide the ideal coastal escape. 5.	Visit the National Museum of Ras Al Khaimah: Housed in a 19th-century fort, the National Museum offers insights into the rich heritage and culture of the region. From fascinating archaeological finds to traditional Emirati artifacts, the museum vividly narrates the story of Ras Al Khaimah’s past. 6.	Discover Dhayah Fort: Nestled amidst date palm groves, Dhayah Fort is the only hilltop fort still in existence in the UAE, offering panoramic views of the lush landscapes and azure sea. Its strategic position and historical significance make it a must-visit for history buffs. 7.	Enjoy Desert Adventures: For a quintessential Arabian experience, embark on a desert safari. Enjoy dune bashing, ride a camel, or try sandboarding. As the sun sets, the desert transforms, offering a magical backdrop for a traditional Bedouin-style dinner under the stars. 8.	Experience Traditional Souks: Dive into the local culture by visiting traditional souks (markets) in Ras Al Khaimah. These vibrant markets offer a sensory feast of sights and smells, with stalls selling everything from spices and sweets to traditional handicrafts. 9.	Engage in Watersports: Besides lounging on the beach, Ras Al Khaimah offers a range of watersports. Try snorkeling or diving to discover the rich marine life, or rent a jet ski for an adrenaline-pumping ride across the water. 10.	Attend Local Festivals: If your visit coincides with one of Ras Al Khaimah’s lively festivals, be sure to participate. These events showcase traditional dance, music, and Emirati hospitality, providing a memorable cultural experience. How to Reach Ras Al Khaimah By Air: Ras Al Khaimah International Airport hosts flights from various destinations. However, if flying from India, you might land in Dubai or Abu Dhabi followed by a scenic drive to RAK, which takes about 1-2 hours. By Road: RAK is well-connected by road to other emirates. Buses and taxis are readily available for convenient transportation. Quick Travel Guide Top AttractionsGrand Palace: A striking mix of Thai and European architectural styles, this sprawling palace once served as the residence of Siam’s royals. One of its major highlights is the Temple of the Emerald Buddha. Located in the outer court of the Grand Palace, it enshrines the highly revered Buddhist sculpture, Phra Kaeo Morakot. The specialty is that it’s engraved from a single piece of jade. While the palace’s inner court is reserved for royals only, the middle court boasts many attractions worth admiring, such as Chakri Mahaprasat Throne Hall and Sivalai Garden complex, with the Borom Phiman Mansion. Wat Pho: Famously known as the Temple of Reclining Buddha, Wat Pho or Wat Phra Chetuphon is not only popular for being home to the country’s biggest Buddhist sculpture in a resting posture (45 meters long and 15 meters high), but also for its extensive repertoire of stupas, inscriptions, and murals that throw light on the varied aspects of the religion. Built almost 200 years ago, Wat Pho is believed to be the country’s first university and is now regarded as a prominent center of traditional medicine and massage. Bangkok National Museum: Know the varied facets of Thai history with a trip to the National Museum lying within the precincts of the former Wang Na Palace. Exhibiting a vast display of arts and artifacts categorized into: Thai History, Archaeological and Art History Collections, and Decorative Arts and Ethnological Collection, it’s often acknowledged as the biggest museum in Southeast Asia. Wat Arun: Also called Wat Chaeng or the Temple of the Dawn, this shrine – standing splendidly on the Chao Phraya River’s western banks – is a religious site of historical prominence, as it was the site chosen by King Taksin in 1768 to mark the rise of the Thonburi Kingdom after the collapse of Ayutthaya. Erected in the ancient Khmer style, it’s noteworthy for its stunning as well as intricately decorated spire, which, at a height of over 80 meters, is the tallest of its kind in the country. Jim Thompson House: The former residence of Jim Thompson has been converted into a museum. An American architect as well as a keen art collector, Jim Thompson came to the country as part of the Office of Strategic Services during the Second World War, but settled down here, devoting almost three decades to reviving the country’s silk weaving industry, before he mysteriously disappeared in the 1960s. Ringed by greenery and serenity, the house, along with its fascinating collections, offers a glimpse of Jim Thompson’s love for Thai traditional architecture and Asian art. Lumpini Park: Bangkok’s largest public park is situated in the center of the prime business district. With immaculate green spaces, shady trees, artificial lakes, and playgrounds, it’s the place to visit for a breath of fresh air, especially when you get weary of the city’s glitzy sights and attractions.CultureBangkok is a multicultural city. With Little India, Arab Street, China Town, and communes of Europeans and Japanese, you can experience more than a couple of cultures as part of your Bangkok vacation. Combine that with legendary Thai hospitality, and you’ll have an incredible traditional experience, however, without skimping on all the fun effervescent elements. That said, it’s important to dress respectfully while visiting religious sites. Avoid wearing sleeveless tops and shorts, and instead opt for dresses that cover your arms and shoulders. Remove your shoes before entering a Buddhist shrine. No PDAs and refrain from touching or pointing at Buddhist monks, as well as the revered images of Lord Buddha.CuisinePerhaps the greatest pleasure of visiting Bangkok is that there’s no dearth of experiencing the region’s gastronomic bliss. Its varied delights, including spicy papaya salad, shrimp soup, Pad Thai, and green chicken curry, are emulated all across the globe. Savor your favorite cuisines at some of the city’s posh venues or take it easy dining open-air at crammed, colorful streets dotted across Chinatown, Old City, etc.Practical TipsThai is the official language. As a tourist hub, English is also widely spoken here.Thai Baht (THB) is the local currency. 1US$ is equivalent to THB 30.00. Be sure to learn a few basic Thai phrases, such as “Sawasdee” (hello) and “Khop Khun” (thank you).Dress modestly when visiting temples and monasteries.Respect the royal family. Carry mosquito repellent, especially when choosing an activity-packed travel program or visiting Bangkok during the rainy season. Visa & DocumentationWhether traveling from India or Dubai, you can obtain a Bangkok visa with zero stress. For Indian Travelers:Visitors traveling from India are qualified for a visa on arrival with a stay of up to 15 days. But if you’re looking for a longer stay in Thailand, you must apply for the right visa in advance. For UAE Residents Depending on their nationality, UAE residents can enjoy visa-free entry or obtain a visa on arrival in Thailand. Travelers who do not qualify for any visa exemptions are required to apply for a Thailand visa in advance.Documents Required Accurately filled out visa application form A valid passport Recently taken passport-size photographs Accommodation proof Flight booking details Financial proof Rayna Tours Assistance Looking for expert assistance with applying for a single-entry or multiple-entry Thailand visa from Dubai or India? Our knowledgeable visa consultants will guide you through every step until you receive your visa approved on time. Things to do in Bangkok Experience Bangkok’s Rich HeritageBangkok is a land of astonishing charm. Explore prominent Buddhist shrines and centuries-old mansions, or wander through beautiful canals weaving their way across the city, islands, and paddy fields. The historic and religious sites throughout Rattanakosin (Old Bangkok) and Thonburi, including the Grand Palace, Wat Phra Kaeo, Wat Pho, and Sanam Luang Square, offer an immersive glimpse into Bangkok’s captivating past.Discover Quirky Neighborhoods & Modern MarvelsOnce you adjust to the city’s vibrant atmosphere and unrelenting pace, Bangkok’s modern side comes alive. Stroll around Khao San Road’s quirky streets, indulge in retail therapy at its mega malls, or try your hand at bartering at the Chatuchak Weekend Market and exceptional floating markets. Explore Royal AttractionsHead to Bangkok’s royal attractions, including the Royal Elephant National Museum, Abhisek Dusit Throne Hall, and the Vimanmek Mansion, the world’s largest golden teakwood mansion. Each site offers a glimpse into the grandeur of Thailand’s royal history.Reconnect with Nature Bangkok also caters to nature lovers and outdoor enthusiasts. Discover tranquility at Bang Krachao and Suan Rot Fai Park, both perfect for boating, canoeing, and cycling amidst lush greenery. For romantic couples and honeymooners, a dinner cruise along the Chao Phraya River promises a serene and unforgettable experience. Adventure & Adrenaline in BangkokFor thrill-seekers, Bangkok delivers in abundance. Test your limits with extreme cycling at Peppermint Bike Park, skydiving at Nong Kho Reservoir, a full-day Formula Renault driving experience, or rock climbing at Urban Playground. Adventure enthusiasts are guaranteed an action-packed day!How to Reach BangkokThailand’s iconic capital is well-connected by air, road, and rail. By Air: Bangkok’s main airport is Suvarnabhumi Airport (BKK). It operates direct and connecting flights to and from different parts of the world. So whether traveling from India or the UAE, it ensures smooth, hassle-free connectivity. By Road: The region’s well-maintained network of highways makes it effortless for those traveling to Bangkok from neighboring countries, such as Laos and Cambodia. By Rail: Besides a high-end rail network to travel around the country, travelers can also reach Bangkok by rail from countries like Malaysia. Our partnerships with local providers ensure that your excursions are authentic and memorable, with a strong emphasis on comfort and enjoyment.So count on Rayna Tours for the following reasons: Enjoy the flexibility to customize your package to include activities and excursions that suit your interests.Benefit from well-structured itineraries that cover everything from accommodation to activities.Choose from a range of hotels and resorts that fit your budget and taste, from luxurious beachfront properties to budget-friendly stays.Experience the services of knowledgeable local guides. 24/7 customer support ensures that any issues or queries are promptly addressed, providing you with peace of mind throughout your journey.Best Time to Visit PhuketPhuket has a tropical climate, so the weather plays a significant role in planning your visit. The best time to enjoy its charms is between November and April. During these months, the weather is relatively cooler and the seas are calm, making it perfect for beach activities and water sports. For travelers from the UAE and India, escaping the scorching summer heat with a visit to Phuket during these cooler months can be particularly refreshing.Quick GuideTop Attractions:Phang Nga Bay: One of Phuket's most iconic spots, Phang Nga Bay is famous for its dramatic limestone karsts jutting out of emerald-green waters. The bay can be explored via boat tours which often include stops at the famous James Bond Island and sea caves perfect for canoeing.Patong Beach: Patong is the heart of Phuket's nightlife and one of the most famous beach destinations in the world. During the day, visitors can relax on the golden sand, and by night, Patong comes alive with bustling bars, clubs, and restaurants.Phi Phi Islands: A must-visit for any traveler, the Phi Phi Islands offer breathtaking views, crystal-clear waters, and fantastic snorkeling opportunities. A day trip from Phuket, these islands are perfect for those who love nature and adventure.Old Phuket Town: Experience a different side of Phuket by strolling through its historic district. Yes, step back in time in Old Phuket Town, where colonial architecture and charming streets tell stories of the island's rich history. Explore the local markets, colorful houses, and indulge in traditional Thai cuisine at quaint cafes.Big Buddha: Standing at 45 meters tall, the Big Buddha is one of Phuket's most revered landmarks. Perched atop Nakkerd Hill, the imposing Big Buddha is a serene symbol of peace and a vantage point offering panoramic views of the island. It’s a must-see for anyone interested in Phuket's cultural and spiritual side. Wat Chalong: As the largest and most important temple in Phuket, Wat Chalong holds great cultural significance. It’s beautifully adorned with traditional Thai decorations, and visitors can learn about Buddhist traditions while admiring the temple's intricate design.Elephant Sanctuaries: Visit one of Phuket’s ethical elephant sanctuaries where you can learn about these magnificent creatures while supporting conservation efforts. These sanctuaries focus on rescue, rehabilitation, and education, allowing visitors to interact with elephants in an ethical environment.Similan Islands: Renowned as one of the top diving destinations in the world, the Similan Islands offer incredible underwater experiences. The island chain is a favorite among divers and snorkelers eager to explore vibrant coral reefs and diverse marine life.Culture Phuket’s culture is a captivating blend of old and new, tradition and innovation, all set against a backdrop of stunning natural beauty. Phuket has been influenced by various cultures due to its trade history and as a popular tourist destination. Whether you’re exploring ancient temples, participating in lively festivals, or tasting the diverse culinary offerings, Phuket promises a rich cultural experience that leaves a lasting impression. Cuisine:Phuket is not only a feast for the eyes with its stunning natural landscapes and vibrant cultural tapestry but also a paradise for food enthusiasts. The island's cuisine is a delightful fusion of flavors, blending traditional Thai dishes with influences from Chinese, Malay, and Peranakan cultures. When visiting Phuket, you'll discover a culinary journey that's as diverse as it is delicious. Here’s what you can expect when it comes to its dining landscape. From the spicy and tangy Tom Yum Goong (spicy shrimp soup) to the rich and creamy Massaman curry, each dish is crafted with a careful balance of fresh ingredients, herbs, and spices. Street food is also a quintessential part of the local dining experience, with favorites like Pad Thai and Som Tam (green papaya salad) available in vibrant markets and roadside stalls.Practical TipsThe official currency is the Thai Baht (THB). It's advisable to carry some cash for smaller purchases, but credit cards are widely accepted at hotels and larger restaurants.Obtaining travel insurance is highly recommended for covering unexpected medical expenses, cancellations, and other unforeseen events.Songthaews (shared taxis) and tuk-tuks are popular options to get around in the area. Negotiate fares beforehand to avoid overpaying.While English is spoken in tourist areas, learning a few basic Thai phrases can enhance interactions with locals.Respect local customs by dressing modestly when away from the beaches, especially when visiting temples or rural areas.The Thai people hold the monarchy and Buddhism in high esteem. Show respect by not climbing on Buddha statues and standing during the national anthem.Visa & DocumentationFor Indians: Indian nationals require a visa to enter Thailand, which can be obtained on arrival (for a stay of up to 15 days) or in advance for the extended stay. For UAE Citizens and UAE Residents: UAE citizens are granted a 30-day visa exemption if entering by air, while longer stays might require a pre-arranged visa. For UAE residents, they’re eligible for a visa on arrival (depending on their nationalities) or will be required to apply for the right visa for longer stays. DocumentsIt's vital to ensure that your passport is valid for at least six months and carry all necessary documentation, including hotel bookings and travel insurance.Rayna Tours AssistanceFrom the initial consultation to document preparation and submission, Rayna Tours handles every aspect of the visa application process. This comprehensive approach minimizes errors and increases the likelihood a successful application. Top Things to Do in PhuketPhuket, Thailand’s largest island, is a tropical paradise known for its stunning beaches, vibrant nightlife, and rich cultural heritage. Whether you're seeking adventure, relaxation, or a cultural experience, Phuket offers a wide array of activities that cater to every type of traveler. Here’s a guide to some of the top things to do in Phuket.Explore the Beaches: Phuket is home to a plethora of beautiful beaches, each with its own unique charm. Patong Beach is famous for its vibrant nightlife and bustling atmosphere. For those seeking serenity, Kata and Karon beaches offer a more laid-back vibe. Surin Beach and Mai Khao are perfect for those who appreciate luxury and privacy.Discover the Temples: Phuket's cultural side is best explored through its stunning temples. The Big Buddha, which stands at 45 meters tall, offers breathtaking views and a sense of tranquility. Wat Chalong is another must-visit and is the largest and most revered Buddhist temple on the island.Enjoy the Nightlife: Phuket has a pulsating nightlife, particularly in Patong. Bangla Road is the heart of the action, teeming with bars, clubs, and live entertainment. For a more sophisticated evening, Kata Beach has some excellent lounges and cocktail bars.Experience Island Hopping: Surrounded by crystal-clear waters, Phuket is a prime location for exploring nearby islands. A day trip to the Phi Phi Islands or James Bond Island will offer stunning scenery, snorkeling opportunities, and a chance to bask in the untouched beauty of nature.Indulge in Thai Cuisine: Phuket's dining scene is an eclectic mix of local street food and high-end dining. Don’t miss out on trying local delicacies like Pad Thai, Tom Yum Goong, and fresh seafood. The night markets, such as the one in Phuket Town, offer a real taste of authentic Thai street food.Embark on a Diving Adventure: The clear waters around Phuket are a diver’s paradise, rich with diverse marine life. Sites like Racha Noi and Koh Dok Mai offer some of the best diving experiences in Thailand. Whether you’re a seasoned diver or a beginner, there’s something to explore beneath the waves.Explore Old Phuket Town: A trip to Phuket wouldn't be complete without visiting the historic Old Phuket Town. Wander through its narrow streets lined with Sino-Portuguese architecture, boutique shops, and charming cafes. The Sunday Walking Street Market is a highlight, showcasing local crafts and delectable street food.Relax at Spa and Wellness Centers: Phuket is known for its wellness retreats and spas, offering traditional Thai massages and luxurious treatments that rejuvenate the mind and body. Many resorts include on-site spas, but there are also several day spas around the island that provide top-notch services.Take Part in a Muay Thai Session: Embrace Thai culture by participating in a Muay Thai class. Phuket houses several top-notch training camps where you can learn this traditional martial art, whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills.Visit the Phuket Elephant Sanctuary: For an ethical wildlife encounter, head to the Phuket Elephant Sanctuary. Here, you can interact with elephants in a natural and respectful environment, witnessing these magnificent creatures roam free and learn about conservation efforts.How to Reach PhuketPhuket is easily accessible via air, road, and water. By Air: Phuket International Airport (HKT) is the primary airport, located in the north of the island. It provides direct flights from major Asian cities as well as long-haul destinations such as Europe and the Middle East. Apart from this, numerous airlines offer multiple flights daily from Bangkok and other Thai cities like Chiang Mai and Krabi.By Road: It takes approximately 12 hours to drive from Bangkok to Phuket by car via Highway 4 (Phetkasem Road), offering scenic views and convenient stops. Bus services from Bangkok and other Southern Thai cities are available. The journey may take longer but is a budget-friendly alternative with various classes to choose from. Car rentals are also available in major cities and airports in Thailand, providing a flexible schedule for those who prefer driving themselves.By Water: Regular ferry services and speedboats connect Phuket with nearby islands such as Phi Phi Island, Krabi, and Koh Lanta, perfect for island-hopping adventurers. Many luxury cruise lines include Phuket as a stopover in their Southeast Asia itineraries, docking at Phuket Deep Sea Port. For an exclusive experience, hire a private yacht or join a sailing tour from locations like Langkawi or Krabi to reach Phuket by sea. Known for its stunning infrastructure, exquisite hospitality, and exciting activities, it is a destination that promises an unforgettable experience. This guide will walk you through bespoke Abu Dhabi tour packages, travel essentials, and information tailored especially for Indian and UAE visitors.Popular Abu Dhabi Tour PackagesWhen planning a trip to the UAE’s capital, choosing convenient Abu Dhabi packages can enhance your travel experience, offering everything from guided city tours to exclusive sporting events.Package NameDurationPriceEnquire NowAbu Dhabi Stay And Play Luxury Package2N/3DFrom AED 2435 Per PersonView DetailsAbu Dhabi Grand Experiences with Dubai Day Tour5N/6DFrom AED 3389 Per PersonView DetailsAbu Dhabi Express Getaway3N/4DFrom AED 3615 Per PersonView DetailsAbu Dhabi Explorer And Dubai Iconic Tour4N/5DFrom AED 4100Per PersonView DetailsPackages by ThemeAbu Dhabi hosts a variety of themes and events that cater to diverse interest. Here’s a look at some of the top thematic Abu Dhabi travel packages.Family Getaway Package: Ideal for families wanting to explore both cultural and modern attractions, this package includes visits to Yas Island, Ferrari World, and Warner Bros Abu Dhabi with family-friendly hotel accommodations.Cultural Exploration Package: Dive into Abu Dhabi’s rich history with packages that cover tours of the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, Louvre Abu Dhabi, and Qasr Al Hosn. These packages often include guided tours to help you truly understand the deep-rooted traditions of the region.Luxury Retreat Package: Indulge in luxury with stays at some of Abu Dhabi’s most opulent hotels, such as the Emirates Palace. Enjoy spa packages, fine dining experiences, and private yacht charters. NBA Returns to Abu Dhabi: Basketball enthusiasts rejoice! Packages that include tickets to NBA games held in Abu Dhabi are now available. These often bundle accommodation, transport, and game passes, ensuring you have a courtside experience.UFC 321: Tickets with Hotel Packages: For adrenaline junkies and fight fans, experience the thrill of UFC 321 in Abu Dhabi with bespoke packages. Enjoy premium hotel stays, exclusive entry to fan events, and prime seating at the matches.Why Rayna Tours and TravelsChoosing the right travel partner can make the difference between a good trip and a great one. Our curated Abu Dhabi holiday packages ensure:Seamless Booking: Quick and easy online booking process.Tailored Experiences: Customizable itineraries that cater to diverse interests.24/7 Customer Support: Dedicated team to handle inquiries before, during, and after your trip.Expert Guidance: In-depth local insights and tips to enhance your travel experience.Competitive Pricing: Exceptional value with access to exclusive deals and offers.Comprehensive Inclusions: From airport transfers to guided tours, everything you need is covered.Best Time to Visit Abu DhabiPlanning your visit is crucial to ensure you have the most enjoyable experience in Abu Dhabi. Though the city charms year-round, considering the weather may significantly enhances your travel.Peak Season (November to March): This period is widely regarded as the best time to visit. The weather is pleasantly cool, with temperatures ranging from 18°C to 25°C (64°F to 77°F), making it ideal for outdoor sightseeing and activities. During these months, Abu Dhabi hosts numerous events and festivals, providing visitors with cultural and entertainment options to explore.Shoulder Season (April and October): As temperatures begin to rise, these months offer a less crowded yet comfortable experience. While daytime temperatures can be warm, evenings are generally pleasant, allowing for leisure activities. It's an opportune time for visitors seeking to balance good weather with fewer tourists.Low Season (May to September): Known for its extreme heat, with temperatures soaring up to 40°C (104°F) or more, this period is less favorable for outdoor adventures. However, this is the season for those looking for great deals on accommodations and attractions. Many indoor activities, like shopping malls and museums, provide air-conditioned comfort, offering respite from the heat.Quick GuideTop AttractionsSheikh Zayed Grand Mosque: As one of the world's largest mosques, Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque is an architectural marvel that captivates visitors with its grandeur. Adorned with 82 domes, over a thousand columns, and the world's largest hand-knotted carpet, the mosque can accommodate over 40,000 worshippers. The stunning white marble structure is embellished with precious stones, gold, and intricate Islamic art, making it a must-see symbol of Islamic heritage and spirituality.Louvre Abu Dhabi: Located on Saadiyat Island, the Louvre Abu Dhabi is a testament to the city's commitment to cultural and artistic preservation. This iconic museum, with its striking steel dome and playful interplay of light and shadow, houses a diverse collection of artworks from ancient to contemporary periods. It serves as a bridge between art from different cultures and eras, inviting visitors to explore the shared narratives of humanity.Emirates Palace: Synonymous with opulence and luxury, Emirates Palace is more than just a hotel—it's an iconic attraction in its own right. With its lavish interiors, sprawling gardens, and private beach, the palace offers a taste of royalty to its guests. Visitors can indulge in afternoon tea, explore its art galleries, or simply marvel at the architectural splendor.Ferrari World Abu Dhabi: For thrill-seekers, Ferrari World Abu Dhabi is an unmissable destination. As the world's first Ferrari-branded theme park, it boasts the fastest roller-coaster, Formula Rossa, which mimics the G-force of a Ferrari F1 car. The park offers a variety of attractions, from virtual reality experiences to family-friendly rides, embodying the spirit of the famous Italian car manufacturer.Yas Marina Circuit: Motorsport enthusiasts will find the Yas Marina Circuit irresistible. Home to the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, this state-of-the-art racetrack offers visitors a chance to participate in driving experiences, karting, and guided tours. The circuit's unique design and waterfront location make it one of the most technically challenging tracks in the F1 calendar.Qasr Al Hosn: The oldest stone building in Abu Dhabi, this fort stands as a symbol of the city's rich history and resilience, offering visitors insights into the Emirate's development over the centuries.CultureAbu Dhabi's culture is a rich amalgam of traditions and modern influences. It stands as a testament to the city's evolution from a humble fishing village to a global metropolis. The Emirati culture is deeply embedded in the Bedouin traditions—hospitality, poetry, and falconry—which continue to be celebrated today. Festivals such as Eid al-Fitr and the Abu Dhabi International Book Fair highlight the cultural vibrancy and bring communities together in joyous celebration.CuisineAt the heart of Abu Dhabi's culinary identity is its traditional Emirati cuisine. It's characterized by aromatic spices and hearty ingredients. That said, Abu Dhabi's culinary landscape is as diverse as it is delicious. As a bustling cosmopolitan city, it brings together flavors from across the globe, delighting food enthusiasts with an array of gastronomic experiences. So whether you're looking for a simple street-food experience or a luxurious gourmet meal, the city serves a remarkable culinary journey that caters to every palate and preference. Key dishes include:Machboos: A flavorful rice dish akin to biryani, often made with chicken, beef, or seafood, infused with saffron and a blend of spices.Luqaimat: Sweet dumplings drizzled with date syrup, offering a perfect ending to a meal.Harees: A comforting dish made from wheat and meat, slow-cooked to a porridge-like consistency.Shawarma: Thin slices of meat wrapped in soft flatbreads, commonly served with pickles and garlic sauce.Falafel: Deep-fried balls made from ground chickpeas or fava beans, often served as part of a mezze or sandwich.Hummus and Baba Ghanoush: Creamy dips made from chickpeas and eggplant, respectively, that are staple appetizers.Practical Travel TipsCurrency: The local currency is the UAE Dirham (AED).Language: Arabic is the official language but English is widely spoken.Transportation: Public transport is efficient with taxis readily available.Visa & DocumentationTravelers from India and other countries not eligible for visa exemptions are required to obtain a UAE visa prior to arrival. This can be completed via online portals or through authorized travel agents. Ensure your passport is valid for at least six months from your travel date.Rayna Tours Assistance With years of experience in the travel and tourism industry, Rayna Tours brings unmatched expertise to the table. Their knowledgeable team is well-versed in UAE immigration regulations and stays updated on the ever-evolving visa requirements, ensuring that your application is compliant with the latest guidelines.Top Things to Do in Abu DhabiAbu Dhabi is a city brimming with diverse attractions, from its iconic skyscrapers to tranquil mangroves. Each of these attractions offers a unique glimpse into what makes Abu Dhabi an incredible travel destination. With so much to see and do, planning your itinerary around these highlights is an excellent way to experience the best of this vibrant city. Here's a look at some must-see places and must-do activities that capture the essence of this captivating city.1. Visit Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque: One of the world's largest mosques, the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque is a marvel of modern Islamic architecture. Its opulent interiors are adorned with crystal chandeliers and intricate marble work. A visit here offers a chance to admire its breathtaking beauty and serene ambiance.2.Explore the Louvre Abu Dhabi: An art lover's paradise, the Louvre Abu Dhabi is a masterpiece in itself. This museum showcases an impressive collection of artworks and artifacts from around the world, housed in a stunning building designed by architect Jean Nouvel. Visitors can enjoy a mix of historical pieces and contemporary art under the iconic dome structure.3.Experience Ferrari World: For thrill-seekers, Ferrari World Abu Dhabi is a dream destination. As the world's first Ferrari-branded theme park, it offers exhilarating rides, including the world's fastest roller coaster—Formula Rossa. There's also a variety of family-friendly attractions making it an ideal spot for all ages.4.Relax on Yas Island: Yas Island is a prime leisure destination featuring pristine beaches, luxury hotels, and a vibrant nightlife. You can unwind on the white sands of Yas Beach or embark on adventure at Yas Waterworld. The island also hosts world-class events such as the Formula 1 Etihad Airways Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.5.Discover the Desert: No trip to Abu Dhabi is complete without a desert adventure. Guests can embark on a desert safari to experience dune bashing, camel riding, and traditional Arabian entertainment at a Bedouin-style camp. The surreal beauty of the sunset over the dunes is truly unforgettable.6. Wander Through Qasr Al Hosn: Qasr Al Hosn, the oldest stone building in Abu Dhabi, is a symbol of the nation's heritage. This historic fort has been transformed into a museum offering insights into the Emirate's past. It's a fascinating place to explore for those interested in history and culture.7. Shop and Dine at Abu Dhabi's Malls: Abu Dhabi boasts an array of shopping options, from high-end fashion at The Galleria Mall to traditional souvenirs at the World Trade Center Souk. After shopping, savor the culinary delights at the city's diverse dining scene, which offers everything from sumptuous local cuisine to international flavors.8. Enjoy Nature at Al Wathba Wetland Reserve: For a change of pace, visit the Al Wathba Wetland Reserve, a haven for bird watchers and nature lovers. It is home to flamingos and other wildlife, providing beautiful walking trails to explore the natural surroundings.9. Explore Yas Marina Circuit: Motorsport enthusiasts will find the Yas Marina Circuit irresistible. Home to the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, this state-of-the-art racetrack offers visitors a chance to participate in driving experiences, karting, and guided tours. The circuit's unique design and waterfront location make it one of the most technically challenging tracks in the F1 calendar.How to Reach Abu DhabiBy Air: Abu Dhabi International Airport is well-connected to major Indian cities with frequent flights.By Road: For those in the UAE, Abu Dhabi is accessible via a well-maintained network of highways.By Sea: Cruise liners often make stops at the Abu Dhabi Cruise Terminal.Abu Dhabi offers a unique blend of culture, luxury, and adventure. With a wide array of holiday packages and events, planning a trip to this captivating city is a delightful experience. Whether you’re hunting for thrills, soaking up the culture, or lounging in luxury, Abu Dhabi opens its arms to you, offering memories that will last a lifetime.Explore more with usThings to Do in Abu DhabiTop Events & Concerts in Abu DhabiInternational Tourist VisasCruises from Abu DhabiPopular Holiday DestinationsFull Day Abu Dhabi City TourLouvre Abu DhabiQasr Al Watan Abu DhabiTeamLab PhenomenaQuad Biking Abu DhabiFerrari Theme Park Abu DhabiKidZania Abu DhabiSnow Abu DhabiThe National Aquarium Abu DhabiEmirates Park ZooDownload AppRayna ToursAbout usPartner with usBecome an affiliateGet Help 24/7[email protected]+971 42087112+971 42087112© 2026 Rayna Tours.Built byPrivacy PolicyTerms & conditionsBuilt byDownload AppRayna ToursAbout usPartner with usBecome an affiliateGet Help 24/7[email protected]+971 42087112+971 42087112© 2026 Rayna Tours.Built byPrivacy PolicyTerms & conditionsBuilt by

Whatever your reason might be, you will find your apt tour package with Rayna Tours.Honeymoon/Romantic Package: Couples on a honeymoon or a romantic holiday should go for ‘Enchanting Turkey’ tour package. Here, you get to enjoy a full day tour of the city as well as the Bosphorous along with a leisure day where you can explore the city as per your wish. Hotel stay and return flight tickets are included in the tour package, thus helping you save money.Luxury Escapes: ‘Supreme Turkish Gems’ is the tour package you can choose if you want to enjoy a luxury holiday in Istanbul. The 7 nights, 8 days tour will take you to Istanbul, Cappadocia, and Antalya. Apart from getting the chance to explore all these places in air-conditioned vehicles, you will get to stay at 4-star hotels in all three cities of Turkey. Return flight tickets are also a part of the package.Adventure and Nature: ‘Explore Turkey’ is the right tour package for those who are looking forward to spending time amidst nature and indulging in adventure. After a couple of days in Istanbul, the tour will take you to Cappadocia and Antalaya where you soak in the natural beauty in the form of valleys, waterfalls, and more. You can also go hot air balloon riding and hiking here.Historical Tour: The ‘Charismatic Turkey’ tour is for those who are interested to know the deep-rooted history of Istanbul. The package takes you on a 5-day tour where you explore the Old City of Istanbul along with a tour guide, who will not only take you to all the important historical landmarks but also tell you about them. A tour of the historical city of Busra is also included with this tour package.Why Rayna Tours? Rayna Tours is a reputable travel company with experience of almost two decades. Turkey’s Istanbul is one of the numerous destinations that Rayna Tours offers tour packages to. We have helped thousands of satisfied tourists in planning and executing their Turkey/Istanbul holiday. Here are the reasons you must book Istanbul packages with us:Exclusively curated Istanbul itinerariesBest deals on tour packages with special discountsRound-the-clock local support in Istanbul Quick and efficient visa assistance100% transparent – no hidden costsFully customizable plansTrusted by 100+ happy customersBest Time to Visit Istanbul Before you book one of our Istanbul travel packages, it is important to know the best time to visit the place. The right climate would enhance your experience and make your holiday worthwhile.Spring Season (March to May): The transition season between winter and summer is one of the best times to visit Istanbul. The snow melts and in its place are beautiful blooms and greenery. The temperature in Istanbul is somewhere between 15- to 25-degree C, perfect for cruising and sightseeing. This is also the time when the city hosts the Istanbul Tulip Festival.Summer Season (June to August): Summer is the peak tourist season, as people all around the world flock to the city during this time of the year. Remember that the temperature can go up to 35-degree C during this time of the year. You can expect long, daylight hours, making them ideal conditions for outdoor activities and sightseeing. This is also the perfect time to enjoy Istanbul’s nightlife and the numerous music and arts festivals.Autumn Season (September to November): As summer is the peak tourist season, Istanbul is quite crowded. If you want to avoid the crowd, a visit during the autumn season would be ideal. The temperature drops somewhere between 18-degree C and 25-degree C. You can explore the historical and modern attractions, go on ferry rides, and shop at the bazaars.Winter Season (December to February): Istanbul is low-tourist season during the winter months, as the temperature can drop down to 0-degree C. But if you want to enjoy a white winter among snow-covered landscapes and landmarks, it is a great time to visit Istanbul. Moreover, you will also get to get some good deals on flights, accommodation, and Istanbul travel packages.Quick Travel GuideTop Attractions: Istanbul is a treasure trove of attractions, both historical and modern. Here are some of the attractions that you should not miss when visiting Istanbul.Blue Mosque: Popular for its blue ceramic tiles, the Blue Mosque is one of the major architectural landmarks of the Ottoman Empire.Hagia Sophia: Once a church, converted into a mosque, the Hagia Sophia is an epitome of Byzantine architecture. It also has a museum that tells you about the history of the city.Topkapi Palace: The grand palace of the Ottoman kings, the Topkapi Palace would give you a glimpse into the life of the Sultans during the yesteryears.Dolmabahce Palace: A 19th century palace, the Dolamabahce Palace is the largest palace in Istanbul, located along the Bosphorous. The architectural style of this palace is a combination of Ottoman and European styles.Basilica Cistern: Running under the city of Istanbul, the Basilica Cistern is a large water tank with high ceilings and carved columns, an engineering marvel you must not miss.Bosphorous Cruise: The Bosphorous Strait is what divides Istanbul into Asia and Europe. Going on a dinner cruise on the Bosphorous includes delicious dinner, entertainment, and sightseeing.Galata Tower: A cylindrical, wooden tower, the Galata Tower stands at a height of 63 meters and gives you a panoramic view of the place.Grand Bazaar: Covering an area of 30,000 square meters, the Grand Bazaar is one of the largest markets in the world with over 4000 stores selling varied amounts of products.Culture of Istanbul: The culture of Istanbul is a mix of old and new. Here are some things you should know about the culture of this city of Turkey.As the city lies on the cusp of East and West, you will see the influences of both these on Istanbul.Apart from the Ottomans, you will also see the influences of Byzantine, Roman, and Constantinople cultures in this city.Turkish people are very hospitable and would often welcome tourists to join them for a cup of Turkish tea or coffee.While there is no restriction on outfits, it is important to wear modest clothing in religious places.If you are visiting a local person’s home, it is important to remove your footwear at the door.When you are visiting local markets or bazaars, you can bargain before deciding on the final price.Cuisine of Istanbul: The cultural influences of the dynasties that ruled Istanbul can be seen in its cuisine as well. The Turkish cuisine is an amalgamation of Ottoman, Byzantine, and Roman Empires. Fused with flavors and a variety of spices, the Turkish cuisine is one of the reasons that draws people to Istanbul. Some of the dishes that you must try here are Kebabs, Meze, Menemen, Kofte, Simit, Kumpir, Lahmacun, and more. When it comes to desserts, the Lokum or the Turkish Delight is the most famous, although you must also try Baklava, Dondurma, and Kunefe. Turkish Coffee, Cay (Turkish tea), Ayran, and Raki are some of the beverages to try here.Practical Tips: Here are some practical tips that you need to know about visiting Turkey:The currency of Turkey is Turkish Lira.Credit cards are accepted in most huge establishments like hotels, restaurants, shopping malls, etc. However, do carry cash while visiting small establishments and while shopping in the local markets.Use public transportation like taxis, trams, buses, metros, and ferries while exploring the city. Public transportation is quite efficient in Istanbul.Do not drink tap water in Istanbul. Always opt for bottled water.Be cautious of pickpockets in crowded areas.Cover your shoulders and knees while visiting mosques in the city.Traffic in Istanbul is quite chaotic. Hence, always be cautious while crossing roads.The average daily cost of visiting Turkey can be anywhere around AED 400 to AED 500.Pack your bags as per the season you are visiting. Summers require you to take comfortable, cotton clothes while the other seasons require you to cover up in layers.Turkey Visa and DocumentationAny foreign national who wants to visit Turkey for business or tourism needs to get a Turkey visa. Turkey e-visa is available for those who have a valid USA, UK, Schengen, or Ireland tourist visa or resident visa. This is a single-entry visa with which you can stay in the country for 30 days. All others need to apply for a sticker or paper visa. You need to apply for the Turkey visa through the Turkey embassy or consulate in Dubai. The validity of the regular visa is also 30 days within 180 days. Multiple entry visas are also available.Documents Required for Turkey Visa: When you are applying for a Turkey visa, you need to provide some important documents:Filled and signed application formPassport with at least six months validity and two blank pagesTwo passport size photographsReturn flight ticketsProof of finance like bank statements and salary slipsProof of accommodation or hotel reservationTravel insuranceProof of employmentProcessing Time: The processing time for Turkey evisa is somewhere between 48 and 72 hours, while a regular visa would take anywhere between 10-15 days.Rayna Assistance: Rayna Tours’ visa experts have years of experience in dealing with Turkey visa requirements. Whatever might be your reason to visit Turkey, we can help you get your visa without any hassles. All you need to do is send us all your visa documents, and we will ensure that you will get your Turkey visa on time.Things to do in IstanbulIstanbul is a complete holiday destination, as it has something for everyone. Be it adventure, leisure, or luxury, you can enjoy your dream vacation in the beautiful land of Istanbul.Adventure: If you love adventure, a visit to Istanbul would be definitely exciting.Helicopter tours and paragliding are some of the air tours that you can enjoy here. If you have chosen a tour package that takes you to Cappadocia, you can also go on a hot air balloon ride. Water adventure enthusiasts can have a great time jet skiing or going on a speedboat ride on the Bosphorous. A few other water sports include wakeboarding, paddleboarding, and snorkeling.Istanbul also offers outdoor and nature experiences like rock climbing, camping, hiking, cycling, and kayaking.Luxury: Tourists seeking luxury experiences will not be disappointed, as there are plenty of leisure and luxury activities available in Istanbul.Visiting a Turkish Hamam is one of the most luxurious things to do in Istanbul. This is one of the best ways of getting pampered during your holiday.Rather than going on a dinner cruise on the Bosphorous, opt for a private yacht cruise for a more splendid experience.Go for a private tour of the city, where you get to enjoy the beautiful sights of the city in a more comfortable way.Choose a fine dining restaurant to relish the delicious Turkish cuisine in stylish surroundings.Family Activities: There are abundant family activities that tourists with children can enjoy in Istanbul.You can have a fun time visiting theme parks like Vialand, Bostanci Amusement Park, and Istanbul Aquarium with your kids.Istanbul has several museums that both children and adults would find entertaining. Some of these include Istanbul Toy Museum, Pera Museum, Istanbul Museum of Modern Art, and Rahmi M. Koc Museum.You can spend quality time with your children at the nature attractions of Istanbul. Emirgan Park, Gulhane Park, and Pierre Loti Hill are must-visit attractions with family and friends.Shopping: Just like sightseeing, adventure, and activites, shopping is also an exciting activity in Istanbul. To enjoy a local experience, you must visit the traditional markets or local bazaars like Grand Bazaar, Spice Bazaar, and Arasta Bazaar. Some of the best local products you can buy here are ceramics, carpets, evil eye, jewelry, leather goods, lamps, sweets, spices, scarves, souvenirs, etc. You can also choose to shop at the numerous shopping malls and trendy shopping streets that sell everything from local to international brands.How to Reach Istanbul?Here are the different ways in which you can reach Istanbul from all around the world.By Air: This is the easiest and the most convenient way of reaching Istanbul. The city has a major international airport with flights from over 300 destinations almost every day. There are direct flights from Dubai, Abu Dhabi, and Sharjah to Istanbul almost every day.By Train: If you are in other Turkish cities like Ankara, Konya, or Eskisehir, you can arrive in Istanbul by train. Trains are also available in other countries, i.e. Bulgaria and Romania.By Bus: Regular buses are available from different parts of Turkey to Istanbul as well as cities of nearby countries like Athens, Sofia, Bucharest, Thessaloniki, etc.By Road: If you want to enjoy a road trip, you can arrive in Istanbul via highways through Bulgaria and Greece. This island city-state in Southeast Asia offers an incredible array of experiences, from awe-inspiring skyscrapers to lush green gardens, bustling markets, and a rich culinary scene. For travelers from the UAE and India, Singapore’s blend of cultural familiarity and exotic allure makes it an unparalleled destination. This guide provides a comprehensive overview of what awaits, along with exclusive all-inclusive Singapore tour packages to make your journey unforgettable.Popular Singapore PackagesWith a range of carefully curated Singapore packages, your journey can be both memorable and stress-free. Aquarium, and night rides at Singapore Flyer.Honeymoon Bliss Package: Perfect for newlyweds, this package includes romantic sailings on the Singapore River and luxurious stays at a premium resort with add-ons like a couples’ spa retreat amidst Sentosa's lush greenery.Cultural Exploration Package: Dive into Singapore’s vibrant heritage with guided tours through Little India, Chinatown, and Kampong Glam, tailored especially for visitors from India and the UAE keen on cultural immersion.Why Rayna Tours and Travels Choosing our all-inclusive Singapore travel packages not only ensures a hassle-free experience but also offers exclusive benefits:Personalized itineraries catering specifically to interests of UAE and Indian travelers.Seamless visa processing assistance and 24/7 customer support.Partnerships with premium hotels and restaurants to ensure a luxurious experience without compromise.Best Time to Visit SingaporeSingapore’s equatorial climate means it's a year-round destination. However, visitors from the UAE will appreciate the slightly cooler and breezy months from November to March. Festivals such as the Singapore Food Festival in July and the Great Singapore Sale in June are major attractions. Indian travelers often find the Chinese New Year celebrations in late January or early February an exciting time to visit.Quick GuideTop AttractionsMarina Bay Sands: Marina Bay Sands is an iconic landmark on Singapore's skyline, known for its futuristic architecture and luxurious offerings. This integrated resort features a stunning infinity pool atop its 57-story tower, providing breathtaking views of the city. Singapore Flyer: The Singapore Flyer, one of the world’s largest observation wheels, offers breathtaking panoramic views of Marina Bay and beyond, providing a unique perspective of the city's iconic skyline both day and night. A ride in this giant wheel lasts about 30 minutes, providing ample time to relax and capture unforgettable memories from an elevation of 165 meters.Gardens by the Bay: One of Singapore's most popular attractions, Gardens by the Bay, showcases nature's beauty in a unique urban setting. The futuristic park spans over 101 hectares and features the stunning Supertree Grove, where vertical gardens light up the sky in a dazzling display each evening. Sentosa Island: Sentosa Island is Singapore's ultimate leisure destination, boasting an array of attractions for every kind of traveler. Families will find endless entertainment at Universal Studios Singapore, where thrilling rides and shows bring movie magic to life. For beach lovers, Siloso, Palawan, and Tanjong Beaches offer pristine sands and inviting waters. Adventure seekers can try the Mega Adventure Park's zip lines or explore the vibrant underwater world at S.E.A. Aquarium. With so much to see and do, Sentosa Island is a playground of endless possibilities.Chinatown: Chinatown in Singapore is an engaging cultural hub. Wander the bustling streets and discover ornate temples, such as the Buddha Tooth Relic Temple, or shop for traditional snacks and souvenirs at the vibrant street markets. Satisfy your culinary curiosity with authentic Chinese cuisine at hawker stalls and chic restaurants. Orchard Road: Shopaholics will feel right at home on Orchard Road, Singapore’s premier shopping district known for its luxury boutiques and sprawling malls. From international fashion houses to local brands, Orchard Road offers a shopping experience to suit every taste and budget. CultureSingapore is a harmonious blend of Malay, Chinese, Indian, and Eurasian cultures. Traditional festivals like Deepavali and Hari Raya Puasa are celebrated with fervor, providing a rich cultural experience for Indian and UAE travelers.CuisineRelish the local gastronomic delights with specialties such as Hainanese Chicken Rice, Laksa, and Chilli Crab. For a taste of home, Little India serves authentic Indian flavors, while venues across the city cater exquisite Halal and Middle Eastern cuisines.Practical TipsCurrency: Singapore Dollar (SGD). Situated in the heart of the city, this remarkable structure is not only known for its architectural marvel but also for the numerous experiences it encapsulates. Ascend to the SkyPark at the top for panoramic views of the metropolis, where the infinity pool creates a horizon like no other. This resort comprises top-notch entertainment facilities, such as a world-class casino, several shopping avenues with premium brands, and cultural performances at the Sands Theatre. A visit here promises a comprehensive taste of Singapore's upscale offerings.Explore Gardens by the Bay: Brimming with vibrant flora and cutting-edge design, Gardens by the Bay is where nature meets futuristic concepts. As you stroll through the Supertree Grove, marvel at the vertical gardens which illuminate the night, offering a spellbinding visual experience. The two grand conservatories, the Cloud Forest with its misty waterfall and the diverse Flower Dome, bring exotic plants from various climates under one glass canopy. It's a place where every corner beckons for transformation and inspiration, perfect for those who cherish botanical wonders in an urban oasis.Delight in Sentosa Island Activities: Sentosa Island, fondly referred to as the State of Fun, is a haven for those seeking excitement and relaxation alike. Enthusiasts of thrill will love Universal Studios Singapore with its movie-inspired rides, while the marine explorers can delve deep into oceanic mysteries at S.E.A. Aquarium. Beyond the attractions, serene and sun-kissed beaches provide a tranquil escape, or if you dare, experience the exhilaration of the island's various adventure parks. Sentosa is a microcosm of leisure that caters to families, thrill-seekers, and anyone eager for an island retreat.Discover the Rich Culture of Chinatown: Stepping into Chinatown transports you to a vibrant hub where heritage and contemporary lifestyles intermingle. This cultural enclave bristles with the sounds and scents of traditional Chinese practices mixed with modern flair. The Buddha Tooth Relic Temple is a marvel of religious artistry, while the bustling markets invite you to explore artisanal goods and traditional delicacies. Sampling authentic dishes, from savory dumplings to sweet tarts, here is an adventure for the palate, making Chinatown a sensory experience of Singapore’s rich heritage.Indulge in Shopping at Orchard Road: Orchard Road is not just a shopping destination; it's a shopping paradise. Renowned globally, this busy boulevard boasts an extensive array of shops, from luxury boutiques to trendsetting pop-ups. It's more than just retail therapy; art enthusiasts will relish the public art installations, while food aficionados can discover cafes serving delights to fuel another round of perusal. Every visit allows you to explore not only merchandise but also the cosmopolitan vibes of Singapore, making Orchard Road an essential pitstop for any visitor.Immerse in the Wonders of Singapore Zoo: A trip to the Singapore Zoo offers a chance to observe wildlife in a spacious, environmentally enriched setting. Known for its "open concept,” visitors can see majestic animals roaming freely in carefully replicated natural habitats. Engage with distinctive experiences like the Rainforest Lumina, an interactive night walk filled with mystical soundscapes and ethereal lights. The zoo's commitment to conservation and education shifts a simple visit into a profound appreciation for animal welfare and biodiversity.Unwind at East Coast Park: Escape the hustle and bustle with a visit to East Coast Park, Singapore's urban oasis along the coastline. This sprawling park offers numerous activities for every visitor, from biking along scenic trails to trying out water sports like kayaking. Family picnics on the sandy beaches, savory barbecues, or simply enjoying the coastal breeze amidst lush greenery provide a relaxing, fulfilling day under the sun.How to Reach SingaporeChangi Airport is the major gateway into Singapore, well-connected by direct flights from major cities in the UAE and India. Emirates, Singapore Airlines, and IndiGo offer daily flights with comfortable services. Upon arrival, choose the efficient MRT network, taxis, or shuttle services for transport within the city.By Air: Changi Airport is the major gateway into Singapore, well-connected by direct flights from major cities in the UAE and India. Emirates, Singapore Airlines, and IndiGo offer daily flights with comfortable services. Upon arrival, choose the efficient MRT network, taxis, or shuttle services for transport within the city. The airport is well-connected to the city center via taxis, trains, and shuttle services, ensuring a smooth transition from your flight to your Singapore adventure.By Road: While Singapore is an island city-state, it is possible to arrive by road if you're coming from Malaysia. The Johor-Singapore Causeway and the Tuas Second Link provide road connectivity between the two countries. Numerous bus services operate across this route, offering comfortable travel to and from major Malaysian cities like Kuala Lumpur and Johor Bahru. Visitors can also choose to drive their own vehicles or rent a car to cross into Singapore. This option allows for flexibility and convenience as one can explore Singapore at their own pace. However, be sure to adhere to both countries’ driving regulations and prepare the necessary documentation for entry.By Water: Being an island, Singapore is accessible via the sea as well. Ferry services connect Singapore to the neighboring Indonesian islands of Batam and Bintan. These trips are short and delightful, offering beautiful views of the coastline. Whether you're seeking cultural immersion, culinary delights, or simply a relaxing getaway, Tashkent has something to offer all year round.Spring (March to May): Spring is arguably the best time to visit Tashkent. As the city thaws from winter, it bursts into colorful blooms and pleasant temperatures, typically ranging from 15°C to 25°C (59°F to 77°F). This period is ideal for exploring Tashkent's many parks and gardens, such as the famous Central Park and the Botanical Garden. It's also a great time to delve into the local culture, as various festivals and events celebrate the arrival of spring.Summer (June to August): While summer in Tashkent can be quite hot, with temperatures soaring to 40°C (104°F), it is still a popular time for tourists. The city comes alive with activities, from bustling markets offering fresh produce and local crafts to lively festivals showcasing traditional music and dance. Air-conditioned venues, such as museums and shopping centers, provide a welcome respite from the heat, making Tashkent an enjoyable summer destination.Autumn (September to November): Autumn is another excellent time to visit Tashkent. The temperatures cool down to a comfortable range of 10°C to 25°C (50°F to 77°F), and the landscapes are adorned with rich autumn hues. This season is perfect for outdoor excursions, visiting historical sites like the Khast Imam Complex or enjoying a stroll along the tree-lined streets. The abundance of autumnal produce also means that the local cuisine reaches its peak, offering delectable seasonal dishes.Winter (December to February): Winter in Tashkent is cold, with temperatures often dropping below freezing. However, the city has its own charm during this season, with a dusting of snow adding a magical touch to the landscape. Winter activities such as visiting museums, enjoying indoor cultural performances, or indulging in traditional Uzbek teas and pastries provide a cozy experience. Moreover, travelers looking for smaller crowds and lower prices will find winter an appealing time to visit.Quick GuideTop Attractions1. Known as the religious center of Tashkent, it houses several stunning Islamic structures, including the beautiful Hazrat Imam Mosque and the Muftiate Building. The highlight here is the Muyi Mubarak Library, which reputedly houses the world's oldest Quran, dating back to the 7th century.2. This massive open-air market is a sensory delight, offering everything from fresh produce and spices to traditional crafts and textiles. Don't forget to try some local delicacies such as plov and samsa as you explore the vivid stalls.3. Amir Timur Museum: Named after the 14th-century Mongol emperor, the Amir Timur Museum provides insights into Uzbekistan's storied past. The museum's architecture is as magnificent as its exhibits, with a blue-domed structure housing an array of artifacts, manuscripts, and historical displays dedicated to Amir Timur and his empire.4. Tashkent Metro: Renowned not just as a mode of transportation, but as an architectural marvel, the Tashkent Metro is a must-see. Each station is uniquely designed, showcasing stunning artwork, mosaics, and chandeliers that reflect Uzbekistan's rich artistic heritage. Apart from its aesthetic appeal, it is an affordable and convenient way to navigate the city.5. Tashkent Tower: Standing as the tallest structure in Central Asia, Tashkent Tower offers panoramic views of the cityscape. Visitors can indulge in fine dining at the revolving restaurant while enjoying the sweeping vistas. It's a perfect spot for photography enthusiasts and those looking to see the city from a different perspective.6. Navoi Opera and Ballet Theatre: For an evening of elegance and culture, the Navoi Opera and Ballet Theatre is the place to be. Boasting a repertoire of classical performances, this historic venue hosts stunning shows that are a testament to Uzbekistan's artistic tradition. The theatre itself is a masterpiece, blending Romanesque and Asian architectural styles.Culture Tashkent's cultural background is a captivating narrative of diversity and resilience. Spanning ancient traditions and Soviet influences to modern cultural innovations, it provides an enriching and multifaceted experience. Visitors to Tashkent are invited to not only witness its historical landmarks but also engage with a dynamic cultural scene that reflects the city's unique place in the world. Whether it's the historic roots or the vibrant present, Tashkent's cultural background ensures an unforgettable journey for every traveler.Cuisine Exploring Tashkent's culinary landscape is akin to embarking on a flavorful journey through time and across borders. It offers a delightful reflection of its historical diversity and cultural confluence, rooted deeply in the traditions of the Silk Road and influenced by the myriad cultures that have passed through the region. From traditional Uzbek staples to modern gastronomic innovations, the city presents a delectable feast for the senses that reflects a storied history and an openness to new culinary horizons. Whether dining in a high-end restaurant or savoring street food, visitors will discover an unforgettable culinary adventure in Tashkent. Practical Tips The local currency in Uzbekistan is the Uzbekistani Som (UZS). It's advisable to carry some cash, as credit card facilities might not be available at smaller establishments.Tashkent boasts a reliable and inexpensive public transportation system, including buses, trolleybuses, trams, and the metro, which is one of the cleanest in the world.
